# Sustainability in Fashion and Textiles: Closing the Loop

> An interdisciplinary workshop on how the fashion and textile industry can move
> from linear production to circular systems. It examines circular design, life
> cycle assessment, and digital technologies for transparency, traceability, and
> circularity, alongside fashion exhibits and a closing panel discussion.
>
> It is a **sub-event of Circular Lab** (https://www.unisg.ch/de/forschung/forschung-im-fokus/circular-lab/),
> the University of St.Gallen's research programme for a sustainable circular
> economy in the Lake Constance region — specifically its textiles focus area.

- **When:** Tuesday, 27 October 2026, 9.00–15.30
- **Where:** Atrium, HSG Square (SQUARE, Guisanstrasse 20, 9010 St.Gallen), Switzerland
- **Host programme:** Circular Lab, co-led by the University of St.Gallen,
  funded with EUR 4 million through Interreg Alpenrhein-Bodensee-Hochrhein and
  Switzerland's New Regional Policy; six universities and 30+ practice partners;
  focus areas textiles and agri-food.
- **Language:** English. Registration required, via the ICS-HSG event page:
  https://ics.unisg.ch/eventliste/event-details/events/closing-the-loop/
- **Fee:** CHF 50, covering the full day including both coffee breaks and lunch.

## Programme

- 09.00–09.15 — Welcome and Opening — Andrei Ciortea (ICS-HSG),
  Fabian Takacs (HSG) and Steffen Finck (FHV), who lead Circular Lab
- 09.15–09.45 — Is Circularity Always More Sustainable? Insights from Life Cycle
  Assessment — Didier Beloin-Saint-Pierre (Empa)
- 09.45–10.00 — Fashion Exhibits: Modular, Upcycled, Heritage & Natural —
  Cristina Dan, Jonas Bendel, Simeon Triantafillidis
- 10.00–10.30 — Coffee Break (included)
- 10.30–11.00 — Startup Perspective: Circular Fashion — Cristina Dan (SOLVE Studio)
- 11.00–11.30 — Student Perspective: Modern Fashion for Circularity —
  Jonas Bendel & Simeon Triantafillidis (Albstadt-Sigmaringen University)
- 11.30–12.00 — Change Management & Sustainability — OST (speaker to be announced)
- 12.00–12.30 — Circular Economy Information Systems — Alessandro Giugno (ICS-HSG)
- 12.30–13.30 — Lunch Break (included)
- Deep dive, Digital Product Passport (one block, two talks):
  - 13.30–14.00 — Regulation, Standards & Roll-outs for Apparel —
    Dominique Guinard (spotd)
  - 14.00–14.30 — DPP in Action: Real-World Case Studies for the Circular
    Economy — Moritz Fiertz (FREITAG AG)
- 14.30–15.30 — Panel Discussion with the Audience: The Sustainability and
  Globalization Conundrum — moderated by Simon Mayer (HSG)

## Speakers

- **Andrei Ciortea** — Assistant Professor for Web-based Systems,
  Institute of Computer Science, University of St.Gallen; co-initiator of
  Circular Lab.
- **Didier Beloin-Saint-Pierre** — Scientist, Technology & Society Lab, Empa.
  Environmental assessment of energy and materials systems; digital ecosystems
  for verifiable LCA and GHG accounting.
- **Cristina Dan** — Founder & Designer, SOLVE Studio. Contextual fashion
  designer and researcher; created Omdanne (first circular multifunctional
  collection) and the zero-waste Refashion strategy.
- **Jonas Bendel & Simeon Triantafillidis** — Albstadt-Sigmaringen University
  (hs-albsig.de). Longevity, heritage, vintage and natural pieces; the
  R-strategies in practice.
- **Alessandro Giugno** — Institute of Computer Science, University of St.Gallen.
  Socio-technical systems; information management for circular economy and
  sustainability.
- **Dominique Guinard** — Founder, spotd; co-founder, EVRYTHNG. Web of Things
  pioneer, co-chair of the GS1 Digital Link standard, contributor to DPP,
  EPCIS 2.0 and C2PA.
- **Moritz Fiertz** — FREITAG AG. Digital Product Passport in the Circular Tarp
  programme.
- **Simon Mayer** — University of St.Gallen; co-initiator of Circular Lab and
  moderator of the closing panel discussion.

## Parent programme

Circular Lab research network: University of St.Gallen, OST, ZHAW,
Albstadt-Sigmaringen University, DHBW Ravensburg, FHV Vorarlberg.
Funders: Interreg Alpenrhein-Bodensee-Hochrhein (co-funded by the European
Union), the Swiss Confederation, and the Canton of St.Gallen.

The Circular Lab is an interdisciplinary research and practice network dedicated
to advancing the circular economy in the Lake Constance region. As a central hub
for circular innovation and business-oriented sustainability, the Lab
collaborates with companies, universities, and other stakeholders to develop
practical approaches for implementing circular value creation, particularly in
the textile industry and the agricultural and food sectors.

- Circular Lab: https://www.unisg.ch/de/forschung/forschung-im-fokus/circular-lab/
- More about the lab: https://www.unisg.ch/de/forschung/forschung-im-fokus/circular-lab/mehr-zum-lab/
- Partner network: https://www.unisg.ch/de/forschung/forschung-im-fokus/circular-lab/weitere-partner/
